entries.title: Cubs pitcher Ben Brown will start Friday's game against the Rangers
entries.summary: <p>Two hours after their 8-3 win Thursday, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> announced that Ben Brown will start the opener of the three-game series in Texas on Friday night.</p><p>Manager Craig Counsell said Brown, who started 15 games last season and has been the Cubs’ most reliable reliever this season, was under consideration to be added to the starting rotation in the absence of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/05/06/cubs-matthew-boyd-surgery-knee-meniscus-craig-counsell-wrigley-field" target="_blank" >injured left-hander Matthew Boyd.</a></p><p>Boyd underwent surgery to remove a torn part of the meniscus cartilage in his left knee Thursday morning, the club announced. The procedure, called an arthroscopic partial meniscectomy. Is designed to ease pain and locking in the knee. Boyd is expected to be on crutches for a few days before beginning rehabilitation.</p><p>Counsell said the Cubs anticipate Boyd being out six weeks.</p><p>“We know he’s going to miss six weeks,’’ he said. “That’s what we’re hoping for. Obviously, we’ll see how it goes. I think the important thing is, how much time he misses throwing. The knee’s gonna recover quickly, but how much throwing down time do we have.’’</p><p>Asked about Brown taking Boyd’s place in the rotation, Counsell said: “I think just covering the innings is kind of what we’re thinking about. So yeah, that’s one of the things we’ve talked about, absolutely.’’</p><p>Brown said he would be open to starting.</p><p>“Yeah, whatever it is, just put my best foot forward,’’ he said. “I like where I’m at. So whatever it is.’’</p><p>Brown said he didn’t think it would take long for him to be stretched out as a starter. Counsell said he has made a point of giving Brown multiple innings. He went 3 1/3 innings in each of his first two appearances this season, and has gone at least two innings in 8 of his next 10 appearances. He has thrown a team-high 25 2/3 innings out of the pen, posting a 2.10 while striking out 10 and walking 8. Four of those walks came in his first three appearances.</p><p>Brown began last season in the rotation, but was dropped after a rough outing in St. Louis June 23, when he gave up 8 runs on 9 hits in 5 innings, including four home runs. He made on start thereafter, on July 27, when he allowed just three hits and a run in a 5-4 win over the White Sox.</p><h3>Roster moves</h3><p></p><p>Corbin Martin, who inherited a 4-2 lead in the ninth inning Wednesday and gave up three runs without retiring a batter, was designated for assignment Thursday morning. To take his place on the roster, the Cubs promoted right-hander Gavin Hollowell from Iowa. He had 15 strikeouts in 8 innings in Triple-A.</p><p>Over Martin’s last three outings, he had allowed eight base runners (four hits, four walks) and 6 earned runs while retiring just three batters.</p><p></p><h3>Walk-off wonders</h3><h3></h3><p>With his bases-loaded walk in the 10th inning of Wednesday night’s 7-6 win over the Reds, Michael Busch became the fourth player in franchise history to be credited with a walkoff RBI in consecutive games. Busch singled home ghost runner Dansby Swanson with the winning run in the 10th inning of Tuesday night’s 3-2 win over the Reds.</p><p>Starlin Castro (2015), Ron Santo (1966) and Bob Will (1961) are the other Cubs to have accomplished the feat. Santo did it most dramatically, with two extra-inning home runs, a 12th-inning, three-run home run off Ted Abernathy of the Braves on May 28. 1966, then a 10th-inning solo home run off Billy O’Dell the next afternoon.</p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: 2nd man charged with hate crime in 2024 attack of Jewish DePaul students
entries.summary: <p>A second man faces hate crime charges in a 2024 attack of two Jewish DePaul University students.</p><p>In November 2024, Max Long and Michael Kaminsky were outside the DePaul student center in the 2200 block of North Sheffield Avenue in Lincoln Park. Long, who lived in Israel and was a soldier in the Israel Defense Forces, was wearing a sign around campus that read “Come talk about Israel with an IDF Soldier” when they were approached and attacked by two men wearing black face masks.</p><p>Kasem Noubani, 24, was charged with two counts each of hate crime and aggravated battery. Adam Erkan, 20, was charged with the same counts last spring.</p><p>The men beat them with their fists and either a soda can or water bottle, and Long suffered a concussion, prosecutors said during a court hearing for Noubani Thursday. Kaminsky suffered a fractured wrist during the attack. Long still suffers memory loss and meets with a specialist every four to six weeks to continue recovering, prosecutors said.</p><p>At the hearing, prosecutors laid out their version of events. Noubani and Erkan met up before the attack in face masks. Erkan talked with Long and Kaminsky while Noubani attacked them from behind, DePaul surveillance video showed, according to prosecutors. Erkan fled in a silver SUV and Noubani ran away and threw his sweatshirt and face mask in the trash. DNA taken from the sweatshirt and mask during the investigation matched Noubani, prosecutors said.</p><p>Erkan pleaded guilty to a battery charge in November and identified Noubani as the person who attacked Long and Kaminsky from behind, prosecutors said.</p><p>Noubani was arrested in Arkansas during a traffic stop and extradited to Illinois. His next court hearing is scheduled for Tuesday.</p><p>Months before the attack, Noubani had pleaded guilty to a trespassing charge during the 2024 Democratic National Convention. He was part of a group that breached a fence that was part of the security perimeter during the convention, held during pro-Palestinian protests that summer.</p><p>Long and Kaminsky filed a lawsuit against DePaul last April, alleging the school was negligent and failed to keep them safe on campus.</p><p>The attack took place months after pro-Palestinian DePaul students erected an encampment on campus demanding an end to the Israeli bombardment of Gaza, which had begun after the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks on Israel. Similar encampments went up at Northwestern University and other campuses across the country in the spring of 2024.</p>
